title: Clone Graph
prompt:
You are given a reference to a node in a connected undirected graph. Each node has an integer label and a list of neighbor labels. Return a deep copy (clone) of the graph.

Since this is a coding exercise, the graph is represented as an adjacency list `graph` where `graph[i]` is the list of neighbor labels for the node labeled `i + 1` (nodes are 1-indexed, matching the standard LeetCode representation). Your function should build an internal graph of node objects, clone every node and every edge, then reconstruct and return the clone's adjacency list in the exact same format (a list where index `i` holds the sorted neighbor labels of cloned node `i + 1`), so it can be compared against the original for equality.

examples.explanation: Node 1 connects to 2 and 4, node 2 connects to 1 and 3, etc. The clone reproduces the same adjacency structure.
A single isolated node with no neighbors clones to a single isolated node.
An empty graph (no nodes at all) simply clones to an empty adjacency list.

constraints: The number of nodes is in the range [0, 100]
There are no repeated edges and no self-loops
hints: Use a hash map from original node label to cloned node object so you never clone the same node twice, even when it's reachable through multiple paths.

Do a DFS (or BFS) from the first node: for each original node, create its clone if it doesn't exist yet, then for every neighbor, create the neighbor's clone (if needed) and link it, recursing into unvisited neighbors.
Since the graph can have cycles, always check the visited/clone map before recursing into a neighbor to avoid infinite loops.

solution.approach: Build a simple graph representation from the input adjacency list. Use DFS starting at node 1, maintaining a map from original label to a cloned node placeholder. For each node visited, clone its neighbors, using the map to avoid re-cloning nodes already seen (which also naturally handles cycles). Finally, walk the clone map to reconstruct the adjacency list in the same index-based format as the input.
